article_content: Hobart 'Hobie' Alter, who helped popularize surfing and sailing with his foam surfboard invention and the 'Hobie Cat' sailboat, has died at the age of 80. According to a statement on the Hobie sporting goods website, Alter passed away on Saturday at his Palm Desert home. While the cause of death was not disclosed, the Orange County Register reported that he had been battling cancer for about five years. The statement mentioned that Alter's dream was to make a living without wearing hard-soled shoes or working east of California's Pacific Coast Highway. By 'making people a toy and giving them a game to play with it,' he introduced the world to an outdoor lifestyle and products that brought fun to everyone. Alter was a champion surfer who won the Makaha International Surf Contest in 1958 and 1959, and he also earned three tandem surfing titles between 1961 and 1963. Renowned for his innovations, he was called 'the Henry Ford of the surfboard industry' by Steve Pezman, thanks to his role in large-scale manufacturing of surfboards. He began by carving wooden surfboards in the garage of his family's Laguna Beach home in the early 1950s. When balsa wood became scarce, Alter and Gordon 'Grubby' Clark pioneered the use of polyurethane foam for boards, which were more flexible, durable, and economical than traditional wooden ones. This invention revolutionized surfing and made Hobie a leading surfboard brand. In the late 1960s, Alter turned his attention to sailing, designing a lightweight catamaran inspired by Polynesian twin-hulled boats. The more affordable 'Hobie Cat' could be launched from the beach, introducing high-performance sailing to a wider audience. For his contributions, Alter was inducted into the National Sailing Hall of Fame in 2011. He is survived by his wife, Susan, their daughter, and two sons. His first retail shop, established in 1954 along Pacific Coast Highway in Dana Point, California, later became a renowned hub for surf culture.

Volgens 'n verklaring op die Hobie-sportgoedere-webwerf het Alter Saterdag by sy huis in Palm Desert gesterf. Alhoewel die doodsoorsaak nie bekend gemaak is nie, het die Orange County Register berig dat hy ongeveer vyf jaar lank met kanker gesukkel het. Die verklaring het genoem dat Alter se droom was om 'n lewe te maak sonder om harde skoene te dra of oos van Kalifornië se Pacific Coast Highway te werk. Deur 'mense 'n speelding te gee en 'n speletjie om daarmee te speel' het hy die wêreld bekendgestel aan 'n buitelewe-leefstyl en produkte wat pret aan almal gebring het. Alter was 'n kampioen-branderplankryer wat die Makaha International Surf Contest in 1958 en 1959 gewen het, en hy het ook drie duet-branderplankry-titels tussen 1961 en 1963 ingepalm. Hy was bekend vir sy innovasies en is deur Steve Pezman beskryf as 'die Henry Ford van die branderplankbedryf' omdat hy grootskaalse vervaardiging van branderplanke ingestel het. Hy het in die vroeë 1950's begin om houtbranderplanke in die motorhuis van sy gesin se huis in Laguna Beach te kerf. Toe balsemhout skaars word, het Alter en Gordon 'Grubby' Clark saamgewerk om poliuretaan-skuim vir planke te gebruik, wat meer buigsaam, duursaam en goedkoper was as tradisionele houtplanke. Hierdie uitvinding het die branderplankrywêreld verander en Hobie 'n vooraanstaande branderplankhandelsmerk gemaak. In die laat 1960's het Alter hom op seil gefokus en 'n liggewig-katamaran ontwerp, geïnspireer deur Polinesiese tweeskroef-bote. Die meer bekostigbare 'Hobie Cat' kon direk van die strand af gelanseer word en het hoëprestasie-seil na 'n breër publiek gebring. Vir sy bydraes is Alter in 2011 in die National Sailing Hall of Fame opgeneem. Hy word oorleef deur sy vrou, Susan, hul dogter en twee seuns. Sy eerste kleinhandelwinkel, wat in 1954 langs die Pacific Coast Highway in Dana Point, Kalifornië, gestig is, het later 'n bekende spilpunt vir branderplankkultuur geword.

article_content: Boris Johnson is a bit of a tw*t, I cannot decide between David Cameron and George Osborne, and I do not know the exact size of UK national debt. These were just a few facts revealed by Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg as he was grilled on Channel 4 comedy show The Last Leg tonight. According to Mr Clegg, he has also thought about slapping David Cameron more than 20 times during this parliament and wants to avoid Nigel Farage at all costs. Mr Clegg was subjected to an awkward grilling on Channel 4 comedy show The Last Leg tonight. When asked, ‘Boris Johnson, statesman or tw*t?’ he responded, ‘Bit more of the latter.’ Mr Clegg agreed to appear to convince host Alex Brooker to vote, but was instead asked a host of personal questions. When given a choice between David Cameron and George Osborne, he refused to answer. He was asked to appear on the comedy show under the pretense of convincing Alex Brooker to vote at the next election, but was subjected to a mastermind-style grilling on everything from his relationship with the opposition to the debt crisis in Greece. Asked to give the size of the UK debt to the nearest hundred, Mr Clegg was left floundering, instead saying it was around five per cent. When guessing the size of the Greek national debt, he did little better, underestimating the figure by around £100 billion. When asked whether he liked David Cameron or George Osborne best, he refused to answer, saying ‘David Osborne’ and ‘George Cameron’ before waiting until Alex Brooker moved on. To the question, ‘Boris Johnson, statesman or tw*t?’ he replied, ‘More of the latter.’ When Mr Clegg was given 30 seconds to speak about voting, the Lib Dem leader used one of Mr Brooker’s favorite restaurants—Nando’s—as an example. Asked about the size of UK debt, he was still floundering before answering about five per cent. He also showed remorse over his decision to hike tuition fees, which saw his party slump in the polls. Response to Mr Clegg’s appearance on Twitter was mixed, with some branding him a comedy figure, while others said his performance had been brave. In remarks that helped win over his audience, he said: ‘If you go into Nando’s and you don’t order, then you can’t complain about what you’re given. If you don’t vote, then you won’t get the kind of government you want, so you should vote.’ Mr Clegg also revealed he is kept up at night over his decision to increase student debt, another remark which impressed those watching. However, he continued to defend the decision, adding: ‘I’m not Prime Minister so I can’t do what I want.’ The Lib Dems’ poll ratings never recovered from the decision to increase fees months after the coalition was formed in 2010. With just 100 days to go until the election, the party faces losing almost half of its seats in the next parliament, according to pollsters. Mr Clegg’s election strategists will be hoping that his appearance in front of 1.6 million viewers will help claw back some ground. On Twitter, reaction to his appearance was mixed, with some slating him as a comedy figure, while others said he came across as brave. The Deputy Prime Minister also took part in a gag at the end, where he threw a melon at Mr Brooker, who attempted to kick it with a blade attached to his foot. One user calling himself Craig wrote: ‘It’s ironic that Nick Clegg is on The Last Leg tonight—as he’s pretty much on his last leg in the government!’ While another man going by the handle East Londoner added: ‘Nick Clegg has got some balls going on The Last Leg tonight. Shame he couldn’t show this bravery in, you know, Parliament…’ However, some people also praised the Deputy Prime Minister. Neil Burnett said: ‘Fair play to Clegg going on The Last Leg, good sport. Should happen more often.’ Lee Allen commented: ‘People give Nick Clegg grief, but fair play to him—that was a good interview and the Nando’s bit made sense.’ Mr Clegg also managed to have a dig at David Cameron over the upcoming televised debates. At the end of the interview, he was asked who he would like to nominate to come on the programme next, replying instantly: ‘David Cameron’. But he added: ‘He won’t come alone, though. He’ll bring the Green Party, the Monster Raving Loony, Larry the Cat, everybody.’

article_content: Graffiti depicting Pope Francis as a superhero has received an official endorsement from the Vatican, which shared a photo of the artwork with its 84,000 Twitter followers. The image, created by Italian street artist Maupal, shows the Pope flying through the air with his white cape flowing behind him. The brightly colored depiction shows the 77-year-old Argentine pontiff pointing his fist forward like Superman. He is wearing a crucifix and carrying a black bag labeled 'values' in Spanish. The Vatican's Pontifical Council for Social Communications posted a tweet saying, 'We share with you a graffiti found in a Roman street near the Vatican.' Italian street artist Maupal posed next to his creation, which appeared on a wall in Rome. Pope Francis, widely known for his use of social media, maintains active Twitter feeds in nine languages, with a total of over 10 million followers. In a sign of how he is resonating with the public, Pope Francis is set to feature on the cover of Rolling Stone, with an article titled 'The times they are a-changin'.' He continues to capture the hearts and minds of people across the world with his down-to-earth demeanor and modern outlook. Photographs also show Pope Francis interacting with crowds, kissing babies, and comforting children. Dressed in white robes, he appears smiling and approachable, underscoring his widely praised inclusive attitude. During a recent gathering, the Pope braved stormy weather with worshippers in St. Peter's Square, remarking that he wished he could join them outside—prompting observers to note his empathy and relatability.

article_content: The UK Government and UNICEF recently hosted the inaugural Girl Summit to gather worldwide commitment toward ending female genital mutilation (FGM) and child marriage, two harmful practices affecting countless girls. New UNICEF research indicates that efforts must intensify where these traditions persist. FGM and child marriage severely harm girls, stripping them of their autonomy and denying them opportunities to flourish. UNICEF Executive Director Anthony Lake emphasized that when girls can shape their own futures, it benefits not only them but also entire communities. Currently, in the 29 African and Middle Eastern nations where FGM is widespread, over 130 million girls have undergone the practice, facing severe physical and psychological consequences such as infection, infertility, and even death. Child marriage is even more prevalent, with over 700 million women having been wed as minors, 250 million from before age 15. Numerous high-profile supporters, including Jennifer Hudson, Cat Deeley, Stephen Fry, Rosie Huntington-Whiteley, Melinda Gates, and Dawn O'Porter, have endorsed the movement. Girls married before 18 frequently drop out of school and experience heightened risks of domestic violence, while teenage mothers face greater dangers in childbirth and for their infants' health. Lake highlighted the urgency of local, community-led strategies to break these entrenched cycles. Just seeing these statistics, he said, must motivate us to act instead of becoming overwhelmed. As part of the summit, the first Insta-documentary, 'Freedom Is...,' was released, featuring user-submitted Instagram clips sharing personal expressions of freedom. Globally, contributors from the UK, USA, Italy, Greece, Armenia, Ethiopia, and Zambia responded to the call 'Freedom is...?' to urge viewers to support ending FGM and child marriage. The film contrasts bright visions of freedom with the sobering reality of those robbed of it through forced marriage or FGM. Influential figures like David Cameron and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley have joined the Girl Summit Pledge (www.girlsummitpledge.com), which has garnered thousands of signatures and social media mentions, reaching a vast global audience. A follow-up video, 'Female Genital Mutilation: A Change Has Begun,' is also available for viewing, further shining a light on FGM and child marriage.
translated_content: Die Britse Regering en UNICEF het onlangs die eerste Girl Summit aangebied om wêreldwye toewyding te verkry vir die beëindiging van vroulike genitale verminking (FGM) en kinderhuwelike, twee skadelike praktyke wat talle meisies raak. Nuwe UNICEF-navorsing dui daarop dat pogings moet versnel waar hierdie tradisies steeds voortduur. FGM en kinderhuwelike berokken meisies groot skade deur hul outonomie te beperk en hulle geleenthede vir groei te ontneem. UNICEF se Uitvoerende Direkteur, Anthony Lake, het beklemtoon dat wanneer meisies hul eie toekoms kan vorm, dit nie net tot hul voordeel is nie, maar ook tot dié van hul gemeenskappe. In die 29 Afrika- en Midde-Oosterse lande waar FGM algemeen is, het meer as 130 miljoen meisies dit ondergaan, met ernstige fisieke en sielkundige gevolge soos infeksie, onvrugbaarheid en selfs dood. Kinderhuwelike is selfs meer algemeen, met oor die 700 miljoen vroue wat as minderjariges getrou het, insluitend 250 miljoen voor 15. Talle invloedryke ondersteuners, waaronder Jennifer Hudson, Cat Deeley, Stephen Fry, Rosie Huntington-Whiteley, Melinda Gates en Dawn O'Porter, ondersteun hierdie inisiatief. Meisies wat voor 18 trou, verlaat dikwels skool vroeër en ondervind groter risiko vir huishoudelike geweld, terwyl tienermoeders meer komplikasies tydens bevalling en vir hul babas se gesondheid in die gesig staar. Lake het beklemtoon dat plaaslike, gemeenskapsgedrewe pogings nodig is om hierdie praktyke uit te roei. Hy het gesê ons moet nie deur hierdie getalle oorweldig word nie, maar eerder aanhou werk aan oplossings. Tydens die beraad is die eerste Insta-dokumentêr, 'Freedom Is...', bekendgestel, met Instagram-uitsnitte van mense wat hul persoonlike uitdrukking van vryheid deel. Internasionale bydraers uit die VK, VSA, Italië, Griekeland, Armenië, Ethiopië en Zambië het gereageer op die vraag: 'Freedom is...?' om kykers aan te spoor om FGM en kinderhuwelike te help beëindig. Die film stel heldere voorstellings van vryheid teenoor die swaar realiteit van meisies wie se vryheid ontneem word deur gedwonge huwelike of FGM. Bekendes soos David Cameron en Rosie Huntington-Whiteley het by die Girl Summit-belofte (www.girlsummitpledge.com) aangesluit, wat duisende handtekeninge en sosiale media-ondersteuning ontvang het en sodoende 'n groot wêreldwye gehoor bereik het. ’n Verdere video, 'Female Genital Mutilation: A Change Has Begun,' is ook beskikbaar om te kyk, wat meer lig werp op FGM en kinderhuwelike.

article_content: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has called for a 'religious revolution' to tackle extremism. In a speech marking the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad, which coincided with New Year's Day, he urged Muslim leaders to act swiftly. 'I say and repeat, again, that we are in need of a religious revolution. You imams are responsible before Allah,' el-Sisi said. 'The entire world is waiting on you... the Islamic world is being torn apart by our own hands.' He emphasized a 'revolution of the self, consciousness, and ethics' as vital to rebuild the Egyptian citizen, someone the nation will need in the near future. El-Sisi, a devout man, was elected in May after leaving the military to run for president. He had served as defense minister and led the removal of Mohamed Morsy—Egypt`s first democratically elected President—positioning himself as a more secular choice against extremist ideologies. El-Sisi criticized what he referred to as 'the thinking that we hold most sacred' for causing anxiety, violence, and destruction. 'Does this mean that 1.6 billion Muslims should want to kill the rest of the world's 7 billion people? Impossible!' he said. Though the speech was forceful, analyst H.A. Hellyer noted that el-Sisi has voiced similar views before and that the president's goal may be to empower established religious authorities to counter radical Islamism. 'How credible can such a state-empowered counternarrative be?' Hellyer asked. On Tuesday, el-Sisi visited the main Coptic cathedral in Cairo for a Christmas mass, becoming the first Egyptian president to do so since the revolution. 'We will build our country together. We will accommodate each other. We will love each other,' he declared.

El-Sisi, 'n godsdienstige man, is in Mei verkies nadat hy die weermag verlaat het om as president te kandideer. Hy het as minister van verdediging gedien en die verwydering van Mohamed Morsy—Egipte se eerste demokraties verkose President—gelei, en homself as 'n meer sekulêre keuse teen ekstremistiese ideologieë geposisioneer. El-Sisi het gekritiseer wat hy beskryf het as 'die denke wat ons die heiligste ag' omdat dit angs, geweld en vernietiging veroorsaak. Hellyer opgemerk dat el-Sisi voorheen soortgelyke sienings uitgespreek het en dat die president se doel moontlik is om gevestigde godsdienstige owerhede te bemagtig om radikale Islamisme teen te werk. 'Hoe geloofwaardig kan so 'n staatsbemagtigde teennarrafief wees?' het Hellyer gevra. Op Dinsdag het el-Sisi die hoof Koptiese katedraal in Kaïro besoek vir 'n Kersmis en het hy die eerste Egiptiese president geword om dit te doen sedert die revolusie. 'Ons sal ons land saam bou. Ons sal mekaar akkommodeer. Ons sal mekaar liefhê,' het hy verklaar.

article_content: On Thursday, Afghan officials released 65 prisoners from the Parwan Detention Center, formerly Bagram prison, despite strong opposition from U.S. authorities who insist these individuals continue to pose a serious threat to both local and international security. Afghan Attorney General Mohammad Ishaq Aloko asserted the action was fully legal under Afghan law. The U.S. Embassy in Kabul expressed its dissatisfaction, calling the mass release 'deeply regrettable' and warning that Afghanistan would bear responsibility for any negative consequences. According to Abdul Shukor Dadras, who leads the Afghan Review Board, the releases followed a thorough evaluation of 88 detainee files. However, U.S. officials argue that the evidence was never given due consideration. A 23-page document obtained by CNN suggests that 19 of those released were directly involved in attacks killing or injuring up to 60 U.S. or coalition personnel, while other sources cited by the U.S. military claim some could be connected to incidents resulting in casualties for 32 service members. The discrepancy remains unexplained. Additionally, the document indicates that 25 men were linked to placing or manufacturing improvised explosive devices, 33 tested positive for explosive residues after capture, and at least 26 were associated with assaults that killed or wounded 57 Afghan citizens and security forces. American officials maintain this action violates a 2012 Memorandum of Understanding that obligates Afghanistan to ensure potentially dangerous detainees remain off the battlefield. NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen echoed these concerns, calling the release a step backward for Afghanistan's rule of law. Meanwhile, President Hamid Karzai criticized the U.S. response, reiterating Afghan sovereignty over judicial decisions. He insisted the move followed repeated investigations and indicated that progress in peace efforts remains a priority before he would sign a Bilateral Security Agreement, which would allow some U.S. and coalition forces to remain in Afghanistan beyond the current year.

article_content: David Cameron, who once enjoyed an elite education at Eton, and his wife Samantha are now exploring state secondary schools in London for their daughter Nancy. They insist that paying for private tuition should be unnecessary if public schools maintain high standards. Cameron, the first Conservative prime minister planning to enroll a child in a state secondary, visited multiple institutions such as Lady Margaret School in Fulham, which Ofsted rates as outstanding. The academy, linked to the Church of England, counts journalist Janet Street-Porter, film director Martha Fiennes, and actress Kelly Hunter among its former students. Lady Margaret School enforces strict entry policies, reserving 67 places annually for applicants whose parents regularly attend Church of England services. The remaining spots go to various religious or non-religious backgrounds, while a banding system ensures a broad range of academic abilities. The Camerons also considered The Grey Coat Hospital, an all-girls comprehensive close to Downing Street, which former Education Secretary Michael Gove chose for his daughter. Another option was Holland Park School, one of Britain’s pioneering comprehensive schools, previously favored by political figures like the late Tony Benn. Samantha, who went to the private Marlborough College, reportedly wants Nancy to have a more typical schooling experience. David Cameron has consistently voiced his belief that properly funded state institutions can compete with top private schools and aims to make fee-paying options unnecessary. The prime minister highlighted government reforms aimed at boosting school performance. He praised strong leadership, an improved curriculum, and better discipline as factors that have reduced the number of students in failing schools by 250,000 since 2010. Cameron also defended stricter exam standards, arguing that all children benefit from a grounding in key subjects like English and Maths. Discussing family life, Cameron admitted that Samantha mainly handles the children’s homework routines. He joked that he struggles to supervise guitar practice and keyboard skills simultaneously, acknowledging the challenges of balancing technology use and academic tasks. Cameron also recalled the influence of his former history teacher, Michael Kidson, who used unorthodox methods to keep students focused. Education Secretary Nicky Morgan noted that convenient, high-quality local schools were likewise her own family’s choice. A Number Ten spokesperson confirmed that the Camerons are evaluating various state schools for the next academic year.

article_content: Headline: Two nurses connected to the Mid Staffordshire Hospital scandal were removed from the nursing register last year for creating a fearful atmosphere on their wards. Sharon Turner (44) and Tracy White (47) were dismissed by the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) after serious allegations of bullying came to light. Reports now show that the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) allocated £4,000 to try to overturn their dismissal in the High Court, arguing that much of the evidence was hearsay. Nevertheless, the court upheld the original ruling. Funds from nurse membership fees covered this legal challenge, a move that outraged bereaved families who lost relatives at Mid Staffordshire and questioned the union's commitment to high standards of care. Between 2005 and 2009, as many as 1,200 patients are believed to have died unnecessarily at the hospital, which is now under intense scrutiny and faces a large fine for serious care failures. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt is expected to dissolve the Mid Staffordshire NHS Trust due to its tarnished image. White was accused of falsifying patient wait times, degrading elderly people, and denying crucial assistance, which reportedly contributed to at least one patient's distressing final hours. Turner, meanwhile, was said to show open disregard for patients and manipulated care data. Both nurses were found to have fostered a toxic environment in the accident and emergency unit, intimidating junior staff into producing misleading statistics. The NMC deemed their conduct among the worst it had encountered. The RCN's decision to challenge their dismissal has drawn condemnation from campaign groups, including Cure the NHS. Critics argue that the organization should prioritize supporting whistleblowers and safeguarding patient welfare rather than defending staff ruled guilty of serious misconduct.

Sharon Turner (44) en Tracy White (47) is deur die Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) ontslaan ná ernstige bewerings van boeliegedrag aan die lig gekom het. Daar is nou aan die lig gebring dat die Royal College of Nursing (RCN) £4,000 bestee het om hul ontslag in die Hooggeregshof aan te vat, en aangevoer het dat baie van die getuienis op hoorsê gegrond was. article_content: Passengers traveling with one carry-on item can now use an express security lane at Pittsburgh International Airport. Bradley D. Penrod, executive director and CEO of the Allegheny County Airport Authority, noted that this measure addresses the rising number of people carrying more items to avoid airline bag fees. He emphasized that the express lane streamlines wait times for those who pack light. Opened on Tuesday, the lane is managed by a TSA employee and is located to the right of the airport's main security checkpoint. Travelers with one item – such as a purse, briefcase, or computer bag – can use the express lane, while jackets are excluded from the item count. Any additional items require the regular security lines. According to Allegheny County Airport Authority spokesperson JoAnn Jenny, traveler response has been positive, and many find the concept exciting. She mentioned that Pittsburgh International could be the first U.S. airport to implement this particular idea, though other airports have versions of express lanes for different traveler categories. This initiative is not part of a nationwide pilot program but is instead a practical fix for a Pittsburgh-specific challenge. In previous months, security lines sometimes stretched beyond an hour, so the airport worked with the TSA to develop this express lane in hopes of speeding up the process. TSA spokesman Greg Soule stated that the agency partners with airports across the country to ensure effective security measures. Pittsburgh International expects that the new lane will encourage passengers to pack lightly, especially when holiday travel peaks.

Hy het benadruk dat die vinnige baan wagtye verkort vir liggepakte reisigers. Die baan, wat Dinsdag geopen is, word beman deur 'n TSA-werknemer en is regs van die hoofsekuriteitskontrolepunt geleë. article_content: Johannesburg, South Africa (CNN) -- A South African military plane crashed in the Drakensberg mountains while en route to an airport near former President Nelson Mandela's rural hometown, authorities said Thursday. A military spokesman declined to discuss the plane's mission or the number of people on board, but confirmed that rescuers were searching for survivors. Local media reported that the plane, which departed from a Pretoria airbase on Wednesday night, carried a team of doctors responsible for the former president's health care. However, two sources close to Mandela stated that the passengers were not the anti-apartheid icon's medical team. According to defense department spokesman Siphiwe Dlamini, rescue crews found the wreckage in the Drakensberg mountains, although it remains too early to determine the cause of the crash. The aircraft was headed for Mthatha airport, located around 20 miles (30 kilometers) from Mandela's home village of Qunu. Mandela, 94, has not been seen in public since the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. He receives round-the-clock care following abdominal surgery in 2012 and an acute respiratory infection in 2011. Despite his rare appearances, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate and South Africa's first black president remains a revered figure in the nation. CNN's Robyn Curnow contributed from South Africa and Faith Karimi from Atlanta.

Plaaslike media het berig dat die vliegtuig, wat Woensdagaand van n lugmagbasis in Pretoria vertrek het, n span dokters vervoer het wat verantwoordelik is vir die voormalige president se gesondheid. Twee bronne naby Mandela het egter gese dat die passasiers nie sy mediese span was nie. Volgens die woordvoerder van die departement van verdediging, Siphiwe Dlamini, het reddingspanne die wrakstukke in die Drakensberg gevind, alhoewel dit te vroeg is om die oorsaak van die ongeluk te bepaal. Die vliegtuig was op pad na die lughawe in Mthatha, wat ongeveer 20 myl (30 kilometer) van Mandela se tuisdorp Qunu af is. Mandela, 94, is nie sedert die 2010 Wereldbeker in Suid-Afrika in die openbaar gesien nie. Hy ontvang deurlopende versorging na abdominale chirurgie in 2012 en n akute asemhalingsinfeksie in 2011. Ondanks sy skaars optredes, bly die Nobelprys vir Vrede-bekroonde en Suid-Afrika se eerste swart president n hoog aangeskrewe figuur in die land. article_content: John Collins has challenged Ronny Deila's critics to do their worst, insisting the new Celtic boss can cope with any negativity. The Norwegian manager is under pressure to knock Championship leaders Hearts out of the League Cup at Parkhead, having won only five of his first 12 competitive matches. Three months into the job, the former Stromsgodset coach is still seeking a consistent, winning team selection. Collins, as Deila's assistant, believes the manager is well-prepared for the demands of this intense position. He said, 'I have no doubt about that. It comes with the job. You can criticize him all you want.' Collins does not think Deila has changed much, but rather is learning about his players, staff, and opponents. Collins also feels the manager is enjoying the process and has settled in completely after three months. Working at Celtic in the 1990s, Collins notes how much the club has grown in infrastructure and expectation. Deila has acknowledged being overwhelmed by the public attention, but Collins points out that this environment is very different from Norway. Despite that, Collins says, 'There are not many clubs like Celtic in the world or many cities like Glasgow when it comes to football. He is thriving on it.' Celtic have not performed well in domestic cup competitions in recent years, with an especially disappointing home loss to Morton last season. Deila has vowed to do better, and the League Cup is the first trophy on offer. Collins says, 'We know Hearts are a good team, and they are confident and top of their league. But we want to win every trophy this season, so the League Cup is the first we can secure.' Acknowledging a potentially smaller crowd, Collins insists there can be no excuses. 'We need to be ready and professional, no matter how many people show up. If we want to win the cup, we have to be at our best in each match. We respect Hearts, and I am sure they will come to Celtic Park with nothing to lose.' Meanwhile, Charlie Mulgrew hopes to return from a knee injury soon after receiving an injection in London. He tweeted that he looks forward to training in the next couple of weeks.

Drie maande in die pos is die voormalige Stromsgodset-afrigter steeds besig om 'n konsekwente, wen-beginspan te vind. Collins, as Deila se assistent, glo die afrigter is goed voorbereid op die eise van hierdie intense pos. Hy sê: 'Ek twyfel nie daaraan nie. Dit kom met die werk. Jy kan hom so veel kritiseer as wat jy wil.' Collins meen nie Deila het werklik verander nie, maar leer eerder sy spelers, personeel en teenstanders beter ken. Collins voel ook dat die afrigter die proses geniet en heeltemal gevestig is ná drie maande. Terwyl hy in die 1990's by Celtic gespeel het, wys Collins daarop hoe baie die klub se infrastruktuur en verwagtinge gegroei het. Deila het erken hy voel oorweldig deur die openbare aandag, maar Collins benadruk dat dit heel anders is as in Noorweë. Tog sê Collins: 'Daar is nie baie klubs soos Celtic in die wêreld nie, en nie baie stede soos Glasgow as dit by sokker kom nie. Hy floreer daarin.' Celtic het nie goed gevaar in binnelandse bekerkompetisies in onlangse jare nie, met 'n slegte nederlaag teen Morton verlede seisoen. Deila het belowe om beter te doen, en die Liga-beker is die eerste trofee wat op die spel is. Collins sê: 'Ons weet Hearts is 'n goeie span, en hulle is vol vertroue en boaan hul liga. Maar ons wil elke trofee hierdie seisoen wen, so die Liga-beker is die eerste wat ons kan vat.' Collins sê hy verwag dalk 'n kleiner skare, maar daar is geen verskonings nie. 'Ons moet gereed en professioneel wees, maak nie saak hoeveel mense opdaag nie. As ons die beker wil wen, moet ons elke wedstryd op ons beste wees. Intussen hoop Charlie Mulgrew om binnekort weer na 'n kniebesering aksie te sien, nadat hy 'n inspuiting in Londen ontvang het. Hy het getwiet dat hy daarna uitsien om binne die volgende paar weke terug te keer na oefening.

article_content: 'Kindles may be popular for reading on the move, but traditional books have inspired spectacular buildings to house valuable collections. French photographer Franck Bohbot has traveled the world to celebrate the humble book by capturing the ethereal beauty of remarkable libraries.' 'The ongoing project, House of Books, showcases some of the greatest bibliothèques. Bohbot began in Paris and Rome, and plans to continue his work in Europe, South America, Asia, and North America. He highlights places of learning, where books are kept for decades.' 'Paying tribute to architects, lighting, compositions, and colors, Bohbot captures both contemporary libraries and smaller, more intimate rooms and entrances. This Parisian photographer, 34, began as a set photographer and shifted his focus in 2008 to public spaces, urban landscapes, and environmental portraits.' 'He is best known for his compositions, use of color, and for immortalizing everyday scenes such as swimming pools, city streets, bars, museums, train stations, and barbershops. He hopes to document his discovery of iconic libraries on his website franckbohbot.com.' 'Some featured libraries include the Bibliothèque Nationale de France, the Bibliothèque interuniversitaire de la Sorbonne, the Biblioteca Angelica in Rome, the Bibliothèque Mazarine, the BNF François-Mitterrand, the Bibliothèque du Sénat, and the Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève, among others.' 'Bohbot appreciates the simple pleasure of reading books and plans to photograph many more libraries in the future.'
translated_content: 'Kindles mag gewild wees om onderweg te lees, maar tradisionele boeke het ons geïnspireer om skouspelagtige geboue te skep om waardevolle versamelings te huisves. Die Franse fotograaf Franck Bohbot reis die wêreld vol om die nederige boek te vier deur die eteriese skoonheid van merkwaardige biblioteke vas te vang.' 'Sy deurlopende projek, House of Books, vertoon van die grootste biblioteke. Bohbot het in Parys en Rome begin en beplan om sy werk in Europa, Suid-Amerika, Asië en Noord-Amerika voort te sit. Hy beklemtoon plekke van leer, waar boeke dekades lank bewaar word.' 'Terwyl hy hul argitektuur, beligting, samestelling en kleure eer, vang Bohbot sowel kontemporêre biblioteke as kleiner, meer intieme ruimtes en ingange vas. Hierdie fotograaf van Parys, 34, het as 'n stel-fotograaf begin en in 2008 sy fokus verskuif na openbare ruimtes, stedelike landskappe en omgewingsportrette.' 'Hy is bekend vir sy komposisies, kleurgebruik en die verewiging van alledaagse tonele soos swembaddens, stadsstrate, kroeë, museums, treinstasies en barbierswinkels. Hy hoop om sy ontdekkings van ikoniese biblioteke op sy webwerf franckbohbot.com te dokumenteer.' 'Van die uitgestalde biblioteke sluit in die Bibliothèque Nationale de France, die Bibliothèque interuniversitaire de la Sorbonne, die Biblioteca Angelica in Rome, die Bibliothèque Mazarine, die BNF François-Mitterrand, die Bibliothèque du Sénat en die Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève, onder andere.' 'Bohbot waardeer die eenvoudige plesier van boeklees en beplan om in die toekoms nog vele biblioteke af te neem.'
